tier_reason: First-party README example: @turbo gemm 111.722 us vs single-threaded MKL mul! 117.221 us at 191x189x171, with the benchmark code inline but no CPU model or Julia version; the repo's benchmark/ harness (loadsharedlibs.jl) states compilers and flags but no CPU was named in anything opened, so it falls short of A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README example: @turbo triple-loop gemm minimum 111.722 microseconds (110.5 GFLOPS) vs MKL mul! (BLAS.set_num_threads(1), vendor :mkl) minimum 117.221 microseconds (105.3 GFLOPS) at M=191, K=189, N=171, about 5% faster (derived from page data); the same loop with only @inbounds @fastmath took 4.891 ms (about 44x slower than @turbo, derived from page data). The project's own docs (docs/src/examples/matrix_multiplication.md) say that for C = A*B LoopVectorization 'falls behind MKL's gemm beyond 70x70 or so', and for A'*B it is 'well behind MKL and OpenBLAS' because it does not pack.
corrections.caveats: Single-shape, single-thread micro-benchmark with a margin of about 5%; the CPU is not named (README: 'the CPU I'm running these benchmarks on', Float64 SIMD width 8, which implies AVX-512) and the Julia version is not stated. The project's own documentation (docs/src/examples/matrix_multiplication.md, read from the repo source since JuliaSIMD.github.io is egress-blocked) says LoopVectorization falls behind MKL's gemm beyond about 70x70 for C = A*B and is well behind MKL and OpenBLAS for A'*B (no packing, no memory modelling), so the README win does not generalize to larger matrices; its main measured advantage is over compiled loops (Clang, gfortran, icc, ifort, Eigen). The benchmark harness in benchmark/ (loadsharedlibs.jl, looptests.c/.f90, looptestseigen.cpp) lists flags such as clang -Ofast -march=native and g++ -O3 -march=native for Eigen. @turbo performs no bounds checking and may reorder operations; misuse gives wrong results. The package is in maintenance mode under the SciML Small Grants programme. Julia-only, so it fits the 'then any' language filter rather than C++. Larger-size Julia work with this approach is Octavian.jl (already catalogued).

notes: README numbers match exactly; license MIT (LICENSE: Copyright (c) 2019 Chris Elrod, Eli Lilly & Co), 790 stars, 73 forks, last commit 2026-05-31, not archived. Worth recording: own docs say it loses to MKL gemm beyond about 70x70, so the win is narrow (small matrices only).
